title: Alphabet's Cloud Boom Powers Record Quarter, but AI Spending Spooks Investors
excerpt: Google's parent company posted $119.8 billion in revenue and 82% cloud growth in Q2, beating Wall Street expectations. But a raised capex forecast of up to $205 billion sent shares sliding after hours.
body:
• Alphabet's Q2 revenue reached $119.8 billion, a 24% increase year-over-year, exceeding expectations.
  • Google Cloud revenue surged 82% to $24.8 billion, significantly surpassing analyst forecasts.
  • Adjusted EPS of $9.11 was boosted by gains from equity investments, but core earnings slightly missed consensus at $2.85 per share.
  • A raised capex forecast for 2026 to $195-$205 billion led to a nearly 5% drop in Alphabet's shares.
Key Takeaways
  • Alphabet's Q2 revenue reached $119.8 billion, up 24% year-over-year, surpassing expectations.
  • Google Cloud revenue soared 82% to $24.8 billion, exceeding analyst forecasts.
  • Adjusted EPS of $9.11 included significant gains from equity investments, but core earnings slightly missed consensus.
  • Capex forecast raised to $195-$205 billion for 2026, causing a nearly 5% drop in shares.

Revenue Beats Across the Board

Alphabet delivered a second quarter that exceeded Wall Street expectations on nearly every headline metric. Revenue rose 24% to $119.8 billion, surpassing analyst consensus of $117.1 billion. Net income came in at $112.1 billion, and adjusted earnings per share hit $9.11 — though the figure was inflated by $6.26 per share in gains from equity investments, primarily in SpaceX and Anthropic.

Stripping out those one-time gains, core earnings were $2.85 per share, just below the $2.88 consensus. "Google comes out with a solid quarter, beating consensus expectations, but not by enough," said Brian Mulberry of Zacks Investment Management.

Cloud Growth Accelerates to 82%

The standout number was Google Cloud, which posted $24.8 billion in revenue — an 82% jump from the prior year, sharply accelerating from the 63% growth reported in Q1. Analysts had expected roughly 64% growth. For the first time, Google included third-party sales of its proprietary TPU AI chips in cloud revenue; customers include Anthropic.

The cloud order backlog ballooned to $514 billion, up from $460 billion in Q1 and $240 billion at the end of 2025. That backlog is converted into revenue as new data centers come online and begin processing AI workloads — training models and running AI applications.

"There are many areas where we are still at the frontier. There are areas where we need to improve."

— Sundar Pichai, Alphabet CEO

Search Revenue Meets — But Doesn't Exceed — Expectations

Google's core search advertising business generated $63.3 billion, matching analyst estimates but coming in just below the $63.4 billion some had projected. Total advertising revenue rose to $81.6 billion, slightly above the $81.3 billion consensus.

The in-line search result came amid growing competition in AI-powered search. Google's Gemini 3, released in November, was competitive with top offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic, but the delayed launch of Gemini 3.5 Pro has left the company trailing in the AI coding tools market.

The Capex Problem: Why Shares Fell

Despite the beat on revenue and cloud growth, Alphabet shares dropped as much as 4.7% in after-hours trading. The culprit: a raised capital expenditure forecast. On the earnings call, the company said it now expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capex in 2026, up from its prior guidance of $180 billion to $190 billion.

Cloud Growth Surge
›Google Cloud revenue hit $24.8 billion.

›Growth accelerated from 63% in Q1.
›Third-party sales of TPU AI chips included.

Second-quarter capex alone was $44.9 billion — a 101% increase from the same period last year. The spending spree drove negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion for the quarter. To help finance the buildout, Google announced an $85 billion equity raise in June.

CFO Anat Ashkenazi told analysts the company plans to lease AI data center capacity from other cloud companies to meet customer demand, adding that the move could pressure profit margins in coming quarters.

What It Means for Big Tech and Indian IT

As the first major tech company to report this earnings cycle, Alphabet's results set the tone for Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta, all of which report next week. The accelerating cloud growth and raised capex guidance suggest that the AI infrastructure buildout is far from peaking — a potential tailwind for Indian IT services companies like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, which handle cloud migration and AI implementation work for global enterprises.

Capex Concerns Impact Shares
›Capex forecast raised to $195-$205 billion for 2026.
›Shares fell nearly 5% in after-hours trading.
›Q2 capex increased by 101% year-over-year.
›Negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion reported.

For the Indian tech workforce in the U.S., Alphabet's continued expansion signals sustained demand for AI and cloud engineering talent, even as the company navigates questions about whether its massive capital spending will deliver proportional returns.

Alphabet shares, which had risen roughly 11% in 2026 heading into earnings, were trading near $333 in after-hours sessions. The company remains the second-best performer among the Magnificent Seven tech stocks this year.
